lineage: Provenance: this package FORKS the accepted lead 0a45ddb2 (116.793080), whose own lineage is cbadde77 -> 6ecec8e3 -> cf6d45a8 -> 0a45ddb2; all four are declared as dependencies. Every identity, size, itemisation, bound, cap, price and toy result is restated and re-verified in THIS package; nothing is inherited by citation. This revision (v10) answers the v9 review's three objections: (1) H1's production extrapolation is now supported by an L-stratified exact-coverage census - twenty genuine primes in four growing strata (L = 74 to 295), the exact covered set enumerated on each, the post-diagonal-correction residual shrinking monotonically with L (mean |dev| 0.00361, 0.00244, 0.00170, 0.00127 across the strata) and fitting c/L with c = 0.235, so the fitted production residual at L = 2^51.63 is 6.7e-17; the regime statement is corrected (production scalars do NOT wrap: a < 2^93, w < 2^78, a*w < 2^171 < r, so Lemma 2's rational distinctness holds at the scalar level exactly; the census's wrapping rows - ten of twenty - are a strictly harder regime, and the wrapping and non-wrapping subsets agree at mean |dev| 0.0023 vs 0.0024); the claim's 0.0015 census-informed allowance is the fitted residual at L = 159, i.e. the claim expenses the coverage as if the production walk list were 2^44.3 times shorter than it is; (2) the point scalar multiplication is charged at 662 reference additions with the window table's affine normalisation priced at the standard algorithm's full cost: the prefix/backward Montgomery batch inverts n = 15 values with 3(n-1) = 42 F_r-multiplications plus the one inversion, and each entry's affine rescale x = X/z^2, y = Y/z^3 costs 4 more (z^2, z^3, two divisions) = 60, so 102 multiplications + 65,536 = 104,662 instructions on top of the 1,218,431-instruction window itemisation: total 1,322,593 instructions = 661.3 reference additions, charged 662 (v9's 648 undercounted the batch as 29 multiplications - the prefix pass alone); (3) the preprocessing figure is now the run's computed ceiling 2^115.7363 (the exact integer sum of the baby side, the walk list, the base H-primes and both gap tables, output by evidence.py), fixing v9's truncated 115.7354 which the baby side alone already exceeded.
work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = records + per-node fixed work + comparisons + gap tables + candidate re-walk (including both table rebuilds) + strand starts + segment starts + status tree + base H-primes + walk list + split gaps + candidate multiplications + kept blocks + candidate copy + Lemma 1, with records = 2N x 2000 x (1 + 148/2000), N = 64424840203624563870472181515288576 = 2^64 x L per side (L = 3492477585540061 steps, all w distinct), m = (r-1)/2^20, K = 4980/10000; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. W(2^20) = 138823277198598325615651887091741570 units exactly. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.740733 = 116740733/1000000.
heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is at least 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39226 at the lower bound K = 0.498 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.498 x (1 + 2^-54), N = 64424840203624563870472181515288576 = 2^64 x L exactly). Support: Lemma 4 (the six-fold symmetry and the parity key make the six orbit images of one record share one key and one comparison), the L-entry walk list giving exactly N = 2^64 x L distinct scalars per side, the diagonal collapse K' = K(1 - (L-1)/L^2), the three coverage toys (z = +0.43/+0.94/-1.43), and the load-bearing L-stratified exact-coverage census: twenty genuine primes with 6d | r-1 in four growing strata, the exact covered set C = {b*u/g mod r_t} enumerated on each, the post-correction residual shrinking monotonically with L and fitting 0.235/L (fitted production residual 6.7e-17), with no systematic bias (signed means +0.0005 or below in every stratum; 14 positive, 6 negative overall) and with the wrapping and non-wrapping scalar regimes in statistical agreement (mean |dev| 0.0023 vs 0.0024).

H2 and H2' (supply): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6332) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list (such gaps split into two table entries against the reserve). The base-prime search interval [2^80, F] is sized by the fixed point X = 2^66*2^20*ln(F) (X ~ 2^92.0), so the integrand bound 1/ln(q) >= 1/ln(F) gives an expected supply of at least 2^66 against the 2^65 requirement, the shortfall the Chernoff tail C9 under H2'' (independent membership indicators). Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

Caps C1-C9 (ours, every tail rounded towards the larger probability): C1 comparisons per node - Bernstein for bounded increments, each giant lookup contributing one head-slot occupancy in [0, 64] (the C2 cap) with variance bound 64 mu, evaluated at the C3-envelope worst mean mu x (1 + 2^-9) against the 1.01 x mu cap: per-node tail 2^-938.2, over all 2^84 nodes 2^-854.2; C2 head-slot depth (Poisson 0.388, tail 2^-82.6 over 2^117 slots); C3 node record-count deviations (Chernoff 2^-2971 over all nodes; the deviation's cost is carried inside C1, which is evaluated at the envelope's worst mean); C4 false candidate pairs - a compared pair already agrees on the 84 routing and 33 slot key bits, so false matches cost 2^-75 per comparison, expected N^2/2^192 = 2^39.27, cap 2^44 with Chernoff tail (e mu/t)^t = 2^-5.7e13; C5 true matches, two channels - off-diagonal Poisson(0.498) tail exp(-1.42e7) = 2^-2.0e7 at the 2^20 cap, and the diagonal challenges z = a/a' which abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 (the same single event that would break C4 and C7); C6 candidate sinks (owner candidate lists, tail 2^-3.9e6; generating-node kept-block receive, tail 2^-3.8e7); C7 re-walk key repeats (the retained key already occurs, so >= 5 kept steps need 4 further hits: L^5/(5! 2^768) per chain, 2^-451.7 over all chains); C8 node overflow (capacity 2^33.32 baby records against mean 2^31.63 per node; 2^-20 budgeted for modelling); C9 base-prime supply (Chernoff 2^-1.3e19 at delta = 1/2 under H2''). Together charged 2^-40.

Success arithmetic: 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39226 at the lower-bound K = 0.498, minus the 2^-40 cap union, minus the 2^-20 C8 modelling budget, minus a 0.0015 census-informed allowance (the census's post-correction residual fits 0.235/L over L = 74 to 295; 0.0015 is the fitted residual at L = 159, so the claim expenses the coverage as if the production walk list, L = 2^51.63, were 2^44.3 times shorter than it is; the fitted production residual is 6.7e-17) = 0.39075, claimed at 0.3907 against the 0.39 required.
limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.

H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys, the L-stratified exact-coverage census and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence). The census's production extrapolation is a measured 1/L fit over a fourfold L range, not a proof; the 0.0015 allowance prices the fit as if production L were 159.

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; every shared price (the F_r-multiplication at 383, the inversion at 2^16 by the full binary extended Euclid (four six-limb values, coefficient maintenance included), the projective 4-bit-window scalar multiplication at 662 including the window table's affine normalisation at the standard batch-inversion cost (3(n-1) + 4n multiplications plus one inversion), the Tonelli-Shanks square root at 2048, the modexp at 512) is derived as a worst-case bound in proof.md section 3 with its algorithm, and the cluster model is the accepted lineage's definition restated. The unit convention is the organiser's own normalisation clause: COST_MODEL.md's prices are 'rounded organizer normalization constants ... not CPU timings or exact measured instruction counts' and candidate_prices_allowed is false, so non-group work is charged as itemised instructions over the pinned 2000-instruction reference budget.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.806 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node and the 40-byte linked pool records included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.81.

The per-record charge 148 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 129/122 (a 14.7 percent margin, the same discipline as the lead's 26 percent over its listed 143, where the lead charged 180); it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0523 bits under the accepted lead and 0.0205 under the pending fork entry 116.761224; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K = 0.498 against the lead's 0.52, charge 148 against the lead's 180 at comparable 14.7/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds (the scalar-mul 640 -> 662 window-table normalisation at the standard batch cost); a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
